name: Hi-Fi RUSH
short_description: A wannabe rock star fights a robot corporation where the whole world moves to the beat.
sources: oracle study 2026-10-23 (public knowledge, no store fetch, no game files)
summary: A wannabe rock star fights a robot corporation where the whole world moves to the beat.

identity.core_loop: Fight to the music: attack on the beat for bigger hits, parry on the beat, traverse a level that pulses with the song.
identity.ui_and_game_feel: Snappy, joyful, cartoon-loud; everything bounces in time.

hud_coverage.method: Oracle study from public knowledge of the game, in our own words; not yet measured on capture

information_grammar.note: The world is the metronome: lights, machines, enemies and the cat companion pulse on the beat. Hit feedback shows rating words on screen.

identity.art_direction: Cel-shaded cartoon with thick outlines and comic-book effects.

rendering.source: derived from the art note by rendering_notes.RULES

tricks: Actions pressed slightly early or late are interpolated so the hit still lands on the beat
Cutscenes are animated to a click track at the song's tempo (about three times the work of a normal scene)
Idle loops, enemies and the world all bob on the same beat
motion.lesson: One clock for animation and music: snap the contact frame to the beat and the player always feels on time.

sources.title: Gameranx: how Tango Gameworks pulled off Hi-Fi Rush (citing director John Johanas)
Unreal Engine interview: Hi-Fi Rush was inspired by Shaun of the Dead and Futurama

motion.source: oracle motion study 2026-10-23 (public talks, interviews and breakdowns; no game files)

identity.audio_mood: Licensed rock and an original score; every sound effect lands on the beat.
identity.lessons_for_abbies_world: Make the whole world pulse with one clock. Animation that lands on the beat even when the player is slightly off is the trick.
